column1: # libaom tool-ablation on the PHOTO gap — after palette ruled out (see
# rd_gap_palette_ablation_2026-07-01.tsv), tests whether CDEF or loop restoration (the two
# other headline AV1 in-loop-filter tools) explain the ~8-18% photo gap in
# docs/RD_GAP_VS_LIBAOM.md. Same corpus/settings as the palette ablation, format 420,
# cpu-used=2. 21/22 images (o_7002 timed out mid-run, not needed for the photo question).
# Harness: scripts/rd_gap/tool_ablation.sh + analyze_tool_ablation.py (zenavif bcb3874fbb92).
# libaom: git 632172a4 (aomenc 3.14.1). Scorer: fast-ssim2-cli v0.6.0.
# + = disabling the tool costs MORE bits (i.e. the tool was helping libaom).
# PHOTOS ONLY (families 1,2,3,5,6,8,9), matched-ssim2 frontier comparison:

# -> Both CDEF and loop restoration (SGR+Wiener) are noise-level (<1%, no consistent sign)
#    on this photo corpus at cpu-used=2. Neither explains the photo gap. zenrav1e already
#    runs sgr_complexity=Full + cdef=true at s2 (speedsettings.rs), consistent with this
#    result. The ~8-18% photo gap remains UNEXPLAINED by any single headline AV1 tool tested
#    so far (palette, CDEF, restoration all ruled out; tx-type search for intra confirmed
#    spec-complete by source read of RAV1E_TX_TYPES vs get_tx_set). Remaining candidates:
#    CfL alpha-search bound (rdo_cfl_alpha uses an adaptive early-exit over +/-16, not
#    exhaustive; unquantified), or an aggregate of many small RDO/heuristic refinements
#    rather than one missing/incomplete feature. See RD_GAP_VS_LIBAOM.md for next steps.
